KEY MESSAGE 1...

The upper level low is spinning east early this morning across 
northern New England. It will continue to gradually exit the area 
through the day. Our area will however remain in a cool west-
northwest flow pattern, with one last shortwave disturbance rolling 
through this afternoon. This will keep overcast conditions along 
with a few scattered rain showers in the forecast through the day 
today. Rainfall amounts will be light, less than a tenth of and 
inch, with only trace amounts (or less in NE PA). The highest 
chances for showers will be up across the I-90 corridor of Central 
NY, where some modest lake enhancement could occur as 850mb 
temperatures reach around -2.5C. The precipitation looks to remain 
in the form of rain, except perhaps the highest elevations above 
2000 feet could see a few wet snow flakes mix in. It will reach the 
upper 30s to mid-40s for highs today across the forecast area.

By tonight the rain showers will be shifting north and east away 
from the area; leading to dry conditions areawide after midnight, 
along with partially clearing skies. There could be some patchy fog 
around as weak surface ridging builds in from the Mid-Atlantic. It 
will be seasonably cool with lows in the upper 20s to 30s.

Sunday will be dry and partly sunny in the morning. High clouds 
arrive out ahead of our next fast moving weather system by the 
afternoon hours, gradually lowering and thickening. Any rain should 
hold off until after sunset.

Heading into Sunday evening and Sunday night the aforementioned low 
pressure center is forecast to track across Ohio and Northeast 
toward Lake America by Monday morning. There could be an attempt at 
some coastal redevelopment of a low along  the NJ coast as well. The 
air mass Sunday evening and Sunday night will be mild, especially as 
south-southwest winds bring more warm air advection into the area. 
850mb temperatures hold between +3C and +5C overnight, and surface 
temperatures hold in the low to mid-40s all night. This will keep 
the precipitation in the form of plain rain areawide. Periods of 
rain develop, some moderate to briefly heavy at times and cross the 
area from west to east overnight. QPF amounts between about one-
third of an inch up to three-quarters of an inch are expected from 
this system by the time the steady rain ends midday Monday.

By Monday afternoon, evening and night some colder air will filter 
into the area behind the cold front. West-northwest winds really 
begin to ramp up too, sustained between 10-20 mph with gusts 30-40 
mph expected due to the steepening low level lapse rates and 
increasing cold air advection. 850mb temperatures drop to -7C by the 
early evening hours, then around -8C overnight. This will be cold 
enough to change the lingering showers from rain to snow around or 
just after sunset Monday. There will be a lake effect response, with 
scattered snow showers southeast of the lakes Monday night. There 
does appear to be quite a bit of dry air in the forecast soundings 
above the 850mb level, so not expecting much if any snow 
accumulations from this minor event. Overnight lows are much cooler, 
dropping down into the 20s areawide. A few flurries or light snow 
showers could linger in and around the Syracuse area on Tuesday 
morning, otherwise surface high pressure builds through the day.

KEY MESSAGE 2...

High pressure looks to remain in place for our area Wednesday and 
Thursday, likely bringing dry and partly sunny weather conditions. 
Winds turn southerly Wednesday and southwesterly on Thursday. This, 
along with warmer air aloft will boost high temperatures well into 
the 40s Wednesday, then low to mid-50s by Thursday. This is nearly 
15 degrees above average for early December. There remain some 
timing differences in the guidance by the end of the week and start 
of next weekend. Overall, it appears the next low pressure system 
will once again approach from the Ohio Valley region bringing 
increasing chances for rain later Friday, Friday night and Saturday. 
Temperatures remain very mild both Friday and Saturday in the latest 
ensemble guidance, still in the 50s...but this will all depend on 
the exact timing of a cold front sometime next weekend behind the 
strong low pressure system.
